title: Functional thinking and pure functions
q: What makes a calculation functional, and what is a pure function?
goal: Explain a function as input → result, recognize outside changes, and separate calculation from effects.

title: Lambda expressions
q: What is a lambda, and how do I read the arrow syntax?
goal: Read parameter → body, distinguish defining behavior from invoking it, and recognize expression and block bodies.

title: Functional interfaces: Function and Predicate
q: How does Java know which inputs and result a lambda must have?
goal: Explain the single abstract method contract and choose between a transformation and a boolean test.

title: Method references
q: What does :: mean, and when can it replace a lambda?
goal: Read a reference to an existing method or constructor and check its input/output compatibility.

title: Supplier, Consumer, and operator shapes
q: Which functional interface should I use when there is no input, no result, or the same type on both sides?
goal: Distinguish producing, performing an action, and transforming within one type.

title: What a stream is
q: What is a Java stream, and how is it different from a collection?
goal: Identify source, intermediate operations, and terminal operation without imagining intermediate lists.

title: filter: keep matching values
q: What does filter do, and why does it need a Predicate?
goal: Choose values using a boolean test while preserving their values and source ownership.

title: map: transform one value into another
q: What does map do, and is it related to a Map collection?
goal: Explain the T → R type change and distinguish transforming values from selecting or indexing them.

title: flatMap: flatten nested results
q: What is flatMap, and when should I use it instead of map?
goal: Distinguish one-to-one conversion from converting to zero or more values and removing one container layer.

title: Lazy pipelines and one-use streams
q: When does a stream run, and why can I not reuse it?
goal: Separate a pipeline recipe from a terminal request and obtain a fresh stream for another use.

title: Terminal operations: questions and results
q: How do count, matching, finding, and forEach differ?
goal: Choose a terminal operation according to whether the result is a count, boolean, possible value, collection, or action.

title: Optional: a result may be absent
q: What is Optional, and how do map, flatMap, orElse, and orElseGet apply to it?
goal: Model presence explicitly, transform a present value, and select a suitable absence policy.

title: reduce: combine values into one result
q: What is reduce, and what makes a valid reduction?
goal: Choose a neutral starting value and an associative combination rule.

title: collect and result ownership
q: How does collect differ from reduce, and which returned lists can I modify?
goal: Choose a collection-building recipe with an explicit modifiability contract.

title: Grouping and partitioning
q: How do groupingBy and partitioningBy build category-based results?
goal: Choose a category key or a boolean split and understand a downstream collector.

title: toMap and duplicate-key policy
q: How do I create a Map from a stream without silently losing duplicate keys?
goal: Name key/value functions, specify a merge policy, and choose map ordering deliberately.

title: Ordering, Comparator, and distinct
q: How do I choose result order and remove duplicates?
goal: Separate encounter order, chosen sort order, and equality-based deduplication.

title: Primitive streams and arrays
q: What are IntStream, mapToInt, boxed, and Arrays.stream?
goal: Choose primitive numeric processing and recognize the int[] varargs trap.

title: Function composition
q: What do andThen and compose mean?
goal: Combine reusable transformations in a deliberate order and check compatible types.

title: Captured variables and effectively final
q: Why can a lambda read a local variable but not reassign it?
goal: Explain captured local values and distinguish final references from immutable objects.

title: Exceptions at functional boundaries
q: Why do checked exceptions not fit every lambda?
goal: Match a lambda to its throws contract and choose a visible failure policy.

title: Side effects, non-interference, and peek
q: Why is changing shared state inside a stream risky?
goal: Keep transformation separate from effects and understand the limits of peek-based debugging.

title: Parallel streams: suitability and limits
q: Does parallelStream automatically make code faster or safer?
goal: Explain splitting/combining work and decide when sequential processing is the better default.

title: Streams that own resources
q: Why must a file-backed stream be closed?
goal: Distinguish in-memory sources from open resources and use try-with-resources.

title: Bounded and prefix-based pipelines
q: How do limit, skip, takeWhile, and dropWhile control which part of a stream is used?
goal: Recognize finite bounds and distinguish prefix rules from filtering.

title: mapMulti: emit zero or more results
q: How does mapMulti differ from map and flatMap?
goal: Compare returned single values, returned inner streams, and explicit output emission.

title: Gatherers: custom intermediate transformations
q: What are Gatherers, and how are they different from collectors?
goal: Distinguish an intermediate transformation recipe from a terminal result-building recipe.

title: Custom collector contracts
q: What do supplier, accumulator, combiner, and finisher mean in a collector?
goal: Recognize a collection recipe and the ownership rules that make partial results safe to combine.
